= PDFDrive deep dive — pdfdrive.org / .net / .com family (2026-10-13) =

*Ask: deep-dive the three PDFDrive domains and “link:pdfdrive” into
the Yubnub CLI. As with Z-Library (§2 of the companion doc), this is a
provenance/safety dive: PDF Drive is a shadow-library search engine
whose index points overwhelmingly at unauthorised copies, so no live
search command or mirror link is wired into the app. What you get:
what happened to the domain family, why every surviving lookalike is
suspect, and the legal shelves that replaced it in the CLI (`guten`,
`ia`, `ol` — new this round).*

Companion: `docs/zlibrary-apk-ghidra-research-2026-10-13.md`.

== 1. What PDF Drive was ==

A “PDF search engine” claiming tens of millions of indexed ebooks,
monetised with premium accounts. Its own framing (“we host nothing,
we only link”) never changed the underlying fact pattern: the index
was built from, and delivered, copyrighted books without licences —
the same legal category as Z-Library, minus the criminal case (so
far, enforcement against PDF Drive has been DMCA/domain pressure
rather than indictments).

== 2. The domain churn — org / net / com ==

- The service **migrated pdfdrive.net → pdfdrive.com** amid copyright
  disputes; paid-plan features disappeared mid-migration (MobiSystems'
  safety review documents the sequence).
- **pdfdrive.org** has cycled between parked, redirect and clone duty
  over the same period — the three TLDs the user listed have never
  been simultaneously authoritative, which is precisely the ambiguity
  clone operators farm.
- **~1 May 2023: the service effectively died.** Download buttons
  across the main domain began redirecting to `#top` / nowhere;
  status trackers and forums converge on “disabled by the devs”
  from that week. Intermittent partial returns (2024) never restored
  a stable search.

== 3. The clone ecology (why no link gets wired in) ==

Every post-2023 “PDF Drive” surface inherits a poisoned namespace:

- Download buttons redirecting to **betting and malware-laced ad
  pages** (user reports on updownradar/Trustpilot, 2023–2024, incl.
  CDN-subdomain virus pages).
- **Fake-VPN coercion popups** (“your carrier blocks downloads —
  install DomVPN”) documented on the .to clone.
- **Un-cancellable “premium” subscriptions**: Trustpilot complaints of
  charges with no working cancel path — card-harvest pattern, same as
  the fake-Z-Library playbook.
- Search broken or index-gutted on most clones within months; the
  name persists because the *brand* still converts search traffic.

Verification heuristic is identical to §2/§7 of the Z-Library doc:
with the original operator gone dark, *any* domain answering to this
name in 2026 is either a squatter, an ad farm, or a harvest page.
There is no certificate, signature or authority record that could
rehabilitate one.

== 4. What the Yubnub CLI does instead (link:pdfdrive, answered) ==

Wired this round (registry 100 → 102, all HTTPS, tests 8/8):

| Command | Shelf | Why it replaces a pdfdrive search |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `guten` | Project Gutenberg search | Public-domain full texts, direct files, zero clone risk |
| `ia` | Internet Archive catalog search | Texts + audio + film + software; controlled lending for in-copyright |
| `ol` | Open Library (already present) | Per-edition records; correct PD/lending status per country |

And the cross-links now exist in both directions: the Z-Library doc's
§5 legal shelves and this doc §4 name the same three commands, and
both docs are linked from each other — the “link:pdfdrive” trail
leads to the research, not to a clone.

== 5. Sources (2026-10-13) ==

web_search reporting: MobiSystems “Is PDF Drive Safe” (net→com
migration, feature loss), PDFExtra safety review (domain history,
copyright posture), r/Piracy May-2023 breakage threads (downloads
dead from ~2023-05-01; DomVPN popup on clone), updownradar
pdfdrive.com status comments (ad/virus redirects via CDN subdomains),
Trustpilot pdfdrive.com reviews (subscription-cancellation failures,
“viruses and ads” since May 2023), 2024 “is it back” threads (search
still broken). Domain claims are reported speech from those sources,
not first-party verification — by design, the live domains were not
visited for this research.
